decisions.approvalNote: User approved Option 1 in the recommended manner: an isolated portable LanceDB artifact package plus automatic managed dependency setup and first-RAG-use repair with notifications.
decisions.context: LanceDB is an embedded Python library whose local database is a directory, while the existing Context save/discard, object-store, publish, download, binding, and digest lifecycle operates on one atomic file. The selected option also determines offline behavior, installer size, storage contract scope, and security testing.

options.label: Portable package with managed download
options.summary: Create a deterministic fixed-layout LanceDB package as one saved artifact and install an exact reviewed LanceDB Python dependency automatically through the existing managed runtime setup, with an idempotent first-RAG-use repair and notification flow.
tradeoffs: Preserves the existing single-blob atomic save, publish, delete, backup, digest, and workspace-binding lifecycle

consequences: Packaging and release pipelines become responsible for carrying and verifying the correct wheelhouse per OS and architecture

options.label: Portable package with bundled wheel
options.summary: Use the same deterministic single-file LanceDB package, but bundle a reviewed platform-specific LanceDB wheel and its required dependency set with each desktop/server distribution for offline installation.
tradeoffs: Works without network access during setup and first use

consequences: Requires new structured-storage contracts, prefix authorization, atomic commit metadata, recursive delete/compensation, and publisher support

options.label: Native directory storage
options.summary: Store every LanceDB directory member as a workspace-scoped multi-object artifact prefix and teach catalog, binding, publish, download, delete, and query flows to treat that prefix atomically.
tradeoffs: Avoids packaging and extraction for local queries
Broadens the artifact store from single blobs to transactional multi-object collections

constraints: Replace only RAG database artifact creation, inspection, and query storage; do not change unrelated SQLite use or Markdown Context Pack ZIP/Markdown behavior.
Do not implement SQLite RAG migration or compatibility because the software has no deployed users; old SQLite RAG media types must fail clearly rather than being silently interpreted or migrated.

Preserve existing chunking, source checks, embeddings, exact lineage and citations, review/save/discard lifecycle, Context Browser behavior, workspace authorization, cancellation, bounded progress, and desktop/server/thin-client parity.
Keep LanceDB embedded and local; do not add a remote vector service or require a separate process.
The user must not manually install LanceDB: the managed dependency path installs it by default with the other runtime libraries and ensures or repairs it before first RAG use if absent.
Notify the user with bounded, path-free status while LanceDB is being installed and report actionable sanitized failure without exposing package-manager output or local paths.
Capability or readiness reads must remain side-effect free and must not install packages.
Use exact reviewed dependency versions and update dependency inventory, license, provenance, SBOM guidance, packaging inputs, and security checks in the same change.
Retain a single atomic saved-artifact lifecycle unless an explicitly approved option changes the object-storage contract.

Run focused denial and failure-path tests while iterating, then the AI roadmap all-suite and required architecture, documentation, dependency-security, server, and thin-client gates once after all increments.

discovery.summary: The existing Context Management RAG path is intentionally isolated behind fixed media-type contracts and the managed Python runtime, but its saved candidate lifecycle is a single-file blob while native LanceDB storage is directory-backed. The existing Python dependency setup already probes and repairs reviewed packages in the managed environment, and Context generation already publishes authoritative task progress to notifications. A production replacement therefore needs an explicit portable artifact representation plus a bounded, host-owned LanceDB dependency ensure path; it must not alter unrelated SQLite usage or Markdown Context Pack storage.

feedback.nextAction: Define per-artifact storage, connection ownership, bounded connection/cache lifetime, concurrent read behavior, and tests so a future system runtime can share the Python worker without sharing tenant data or requiring a process per database.
feedback.summary: Future user-built systems may use different RAG databases concurrently. The LanceDB replacement must not create one global mutable database or singleton connection; every saved RAG artifact remains an isolated workspace-authorized database identity that can be opened independently by the shared Python runtime.

Run only the changed Context worker/application/UI/E2E and three Context AI E2E tests during implementation, using tiny fixtures and local models.

Physically remove or isolate LanceDB from a test managed environment, observe automatic setup/first-use installation and notification state, generate/query independent tiny RAG artifacts, and verify subsequent offline use.

After both increments are implemented, run npm run docs:check, npm run agent-support:check, npm run architecture:check, npm run security:dependencies, npm run build:server, npm run build:thin-client, npm test, npm run test:e2e, and npm run test:all exactly once at the roadmap completion boundary.

workPackages.outcome: An exact reviewed LanceDB dependency and inventory are probed, installed, re-verified, and diagnosed only inside the managed Python environment using a serialized, idempotent, bounded host-owned ensure path.
